$comment: The $id base (https://placeholder.invalid/cytoscape/schemas/) is a placeholder: round 46, the documentation site, decides where the schemas are served. Schemas reference each other by relative filename, so only the base changes then.
title: Cytoscape.js element definition
description: One element in the definition form (v3-style JSON), as accepted by `cytoscape( { elements } )`, `cy.add()`, `cy.patch()` and each chunk of `cy.load()`, and as written by `ele.json()`. Describes cytoscape 4.0.0-unstable. The group is inferred from `data.source` and `data.target` when omitted; an explicit `group` must be 'nodes' or 'edges', and an explicit edge must name both endpoints. Keys the library does not read (v3's `classes` and `scratch`, `ele.json()`'s `removed`) are ignored, not refused, so the schema leaves the object open. What stays the library's job: unique ids, endpoints and parents that name existing nodes.

group.description: 'nodes' or 'edges'. Inferred when omitted: an element whose data names both a source and a target is an edge, anything else a node.

position.description: Nodes only: the model position. A compound parent's position derives from its children.

pannable.description: Dragging this element pans the graph instead (default: true for edges, false for nodes).

data.description: The element's data. `id` is the element's id (generated when omitted); `source` and `target` are an edge's endpoints; `parent` is a node's compound parent. Any other key lands in the `data()` sidecar.

source.description: Edges only: the source node's id.

target.description: Edges only: the target node's id.

parent.description: Nodes only: the compound parent's id (a number is coerced to a string id, as in v3).

edgeData.description: An edge's data: both endpoints are required.
